      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "whether the performance cost of making the inner vector a shared pointer was benchmarked for current regular scripts",
      "quote": "Did you benchmark the cost of making the inner vector a shared pointer for current regular scripts?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author provided benchmark results showing differences within noise except for a regression on VerifyNestedIfScript, and later benchmarked an intrusive ref-counter",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:6588770303",
        "c:6615333954",
        "c:6624074329"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6588770303",
      "status_by_quote": "I used the existing benchmarks and the delta is negligible or better for regular scripts."
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5735860679",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "turn the stack element into a standalone class that is either a prevector or a shared_ptr depending on element size",
      "quote": "I think we can do better by turning the stack element into a standalone class that is either a prevector or a `std::shared_ptr<std::vector>` depending on the element's size.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author tested a union-based approach and reported it did not perform meaningfully better than an intrusive ref-counter",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:6588770303",
        "c:6615333954",
        "c:6624074329"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6624074329",
      "status_by_quote": "after some experimenting with the union-based approach, i could not make it perform meaningfully better than a simple intrusive ref-counter which seemed much less error-prone."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4441488488",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "static elemTrue introduces cross-core atomic contention on the shared_ptr control block in CCheckQueue during parallel script verification",
      "quote": "Wait, doesn't `elemTrue` introduce cross-core atomic contention in `CCheckQueue`?",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "contested",
      "status_note": "author moved them to execution locals, but Yudis-bit countered that this causes two unconditional heap allocations on every EvalScript call; author replied arguing benchmark allocates locals once per ",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4447265267",
        "rc:4460061898"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4449159063",
      "status_by_quote": "Moving them to locals eliminates the bus lock bouncing, but replaces it with two unconditional heap allocations on every"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4441488488",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "wrapping stack elements in std::shared_ptr doubles heap allocations and adds unnecessary atomic refcounting on the thread-local interpreter hot path",
      "quote": "wrapping elements in `std::shared_ptr` doubles heap allocations on the hot path",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "contested",
      "status_note": "author argued benchmark regressions were limited to VerifyNestedIfScript, but reviewer reiterated allocator churn and gave a Concept NACK",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4447265267",
        "rc:4460061898"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4449159063",
      "status_by_quote": "The interpreter hot path shouldn't pay heap or refcounting overhead for a non-existent attack. Concept NACK."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4449159063",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "penalizing existing script evaluation with heap and refcounting overhead mitigates an attack that is consensus-invalid today and should be budgeted by future soft forks",
      "quote": "The 10KB duplication attack is consensus-invalid today under `MAX_SCRIPT_ELEMENT_SIZE = 520`. Any future soft fork that raises element limits must budget its own hashing costs anyway",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained they preferred implementation complexity over arbitrary consensus limits or budget discontinuities",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4460061898"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4460061898",
      "status_by_quote": "We did consider enforcing new consensus rules as a solution... However, we reasoned that additional implementation compl"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4449159063",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "pointer identity does not imply data equality, so pushing identical elements separately bypasses a pointer-keyed cache while pinning dropped elements in memory",
      "quote": "pointer identity does not imply data equality. Pushing identical elements separately creates distinct allocations, bypassing a pointer-keyed cache entirely while pinning dropped elements in memory.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained identical pushes are bounded by bandwidth/fees and cache only needs to prevent cheap duplicate-and-hash asymmetry",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4460061898"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4460061898",
      "status_by_quote": "I don't think we need be concerned with attacks that push identical elements, because such pushes must be paid for by th"
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6602021123",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "stream signatures across multiple <=520-byte stack elements instead of raising the element size limit, avoiding the large-element attack surface altogether",
      "quote": "Another potential direction is to have the (proposed sigop) opcode read from multiple stack elements instead of one.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "contested",
      "status_note": "author argued chunking pushes complexity to wallets, but reviewer countered that splitting schemes into separate taproot leaves makes chunking manageable; author replied explaining it breaks multisig scripts",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:6615333954",
        "c:6637076248"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6635429504",
      "status_by_quote": "splitting actually makes it okayish... I think this is a far smaller thing to reason about than multi-KB elements across the whole interpreter (it has a wider scope)."
    }
  ],
  "support": [],
  "notes": "Updated claims with author's benchmark results on an intrusive ref-counter branch and the follow-up discussion with ismaelsadeeq regarding signature chunking and taproot leaf separation.",
  "waiting_on": [
    {

    },

      "on": "reviewer",
      "what": "response to author's explanation of why signature chunking across separate taproot leaves complicates multisig scripting",
      "id": "c:6637076248"
    }
  ]
}
